subject: Aventis Labs — Dedicated go-live acceptance & runbook
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Lara Jennings <lara@aventislabs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing conversation — next steps for dedicated capacity

Hi Lara — great speaking earlier. Per our call I sketched an acceptance plan for the Hosted -> Dedicated migration and a short data ask so we can validate sizing before a formal swap. Can you confirm the following by EOD Monday?

1) Baseline qps and 95th/99th latency targets for the production traffic you intend to move (hourly distribution if available).
2) Peak sustained concurrency window (minutes) and any batch vs streaming split.
3) Any hard constraints on model family (e.g., only Llama-3 derivatives) or quantized variants.

Attached: initial-sizing-request.xlsx (template for your perf export).

What we propose if numbers match expectations:
- Validation run on dedicated staging fleet for 72 hours (traffic mirror),
- Throughput acceptance: <10% regression on 95th latency vs hosted baseline,
- Cutover window: 4-hour blackout with staged traffic ramp + fallback to hosted.

I'll loop Rishi and Monica to confirm GPU SKU mix and the acceptance test windows.

Thanks — Michael

--
Michael Grant
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Lara Jennings <lara@aventislabs.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Joe Turner <joe.turner@aventislabs.com>, procurement@aventislabs.com
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing conversation — next steps for dedicated capacity

Thanks Michael — attaching our traffic dump and a small note on peak windows. See aventis-traffic-export.csv (attached). Highlights:
- Baseline: 1.8k qps average, 95th latency target 300ms, 99th 450ms at hosted currently.
- Peak: 5.2k qps sustained for ~20 minutes during business hours, spike to 8k qps for ~3 minutes.
- Concurrency: expect 450 concurrent streams during peak sustained window.
- Models: primarily Llama-3-70b-quantized during most flows; some experimental L3-70b-int8 variants.

Questions: what margin do you typically size for burst safety? Also what's the expected lead time for Dedicated provisioning (SKU dependent) — procurement will need that for the PO.

Lara
Aventis Labs
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Aventis traffic export — quick sizing ask

Team — forwarding Aventis traffic export. TL;DR: 1.8k avg, 5.2k sustained peak, 8k short spike, mostly Llama-3-70b quantized. Can we outline a conservative SKU mix and an acceptance window that matches our standard SLOs? Key asks:
- Rishi: can you run a quick bin-packing estimate for H100 vs A100 equivalent capacity with our latest quant rules?
- Monica: need to propose a 72-hour mirror validation schedule and an ops cadence for cutover day (who owns the rollback).

I'll draft a short note back to the customer once we have numbers.

-Michael
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aventis traffic export — quick sizing ask

Michael/Monica — quick calc from infra: using their 95th qps and L3-70b-quantized profile, recommended conservative fleet for initial committed Dedicated:
- Option A (latency-priority): 12x H100 (80GB) with mixed-precision kernels, expected sustained throughput to cover 99% of peaks with 20% headroom.
- Option B (cost-priority): 20x A100-80GB (quantized path), slightly higher queueing under spike but still within 95th latency target if we enforce request throttling on spikes.

Acceptance test plan (outline):
- Staging mirror: 72h traffic mirror at 100% of hosted traffic for a two-day rolling window (broken into two 36h runs to capture weekday+evening load).
- Smoke checks every 4 hours (latency/99th token stability), automated KPI asserts in Redwood Console.
- Cutover: 4-hour window starting 02:00 PT; 0->25% traffic at T+15m, 25->60% at T+60m, 60->100% at T+120m with canary checks and immediate rollback to hosted if any critical KPI fails.

I also recommend we reserve a 24/7 on-call during the cutover: Rishi (infra lead), Monica (CS), and one engineer from customer success.

Rishi
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lara Jennings <lara@aventislabs.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, procurement@aventislabs.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing conversation — next steps for dedicated capacity

Hi Lara — thanks for the export. Based on Rishi's estimates we recommend Option A (12x H100) if Aventis needs strict latency SLAs during spikes. If cost is a hard constraint, Option B will require us to enable request-level throttles during short bursts (we can script ramp policies).

Proposed acceptance & procurement timelines:
- 14 Feb: confirm SKU selection + initial PO intent (procurement can send a soft PO).
- 17–19 Feb: dedicated staging fleet allocation and baseline smoke tests.
- 21–23 Feb: 72-hour mirror acceptance run (we'll provide a checklist and runbook).
- 24 Feb: DocuSign contract goes live for signature (we'll attach runbook and cutover checklist).
- 28 Feb: proposed go-live window (subject to successful acceptance).

Attached: Aventis-dedicated-runbook-v3.pdf (detailed cutover checklist and rollback play).

Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Lara Jennings <lara@aventislabs.com>, Joe Turner <joe.turner@aventislabs.com>, procurement@aventislabs.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Feb 2028 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Aventis — confirmed plan and DocuSign link

Lara / Joe / procurement team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary and next steps:

1) SKU: Aventis confirmed Option A (12x H100).
2) Staging allocation: 17 Feb (team will provision and notify).
3) 72-hour mirror: target 21–23 Feb. Acceptance KPIs: 95th latency <= hosted baseline +10%, 99th token stability within 15% variance.
4) Cutover: target 28 Feb, 02:00 PT window. Rollback policy: immediate fallback to hosted if any critical KPI fails during canary ramp.
5) Contract: please sign via DocuSign (link below) so we can place the order with Capacity — we need signed PO to finalize GPU reservations.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

If procurement can provide a soft PO by EOD Monday (Feb 17) we'll start provisioning. On-call roster for the cutover will be sent 72 hours prior.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Aventis on Dedicated.

--
Michael Grant
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
